First time I had only 1 pool (with a .NET 8 app), now I have 2 system, a new .NET 10 app too. Now BOTH stops. (Prior to this I didn't really have .NET Core apps.)

Issues.Body:
- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [ ] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [ ] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

Load Blazor WebAssembly appsettings in-memory without VFS

## Description

Today, Blazor WebAssembly relies on the runtime to mount `appsettings.json` and `appsettings.{environment}.json` to the virtual file system (VFS), and WebAssemblyHostBuilder reads them using File.Exists and File.ReadAllBytes. This forces Blazor WebAssembly scenarios to touch the VFS during startup even when the user application does not otherwise require VFS.

This change:
1. Adds WebAssemblyConfigLoader in Web.JS, running during onConfigLoaded. It fetches the appsettings files in-memory via fetch (honoring custom resource loaders if specified) and exposes them through Blazor._internal.getConfig.
2. Deletes loadedConfig.appsettings in JS so that dotnet.js does not fetch or mount them to the VFS.
3. Re-introduces the GetConfig [JSImport] on InternalJSImportMethods.
4. Updates WebAssemblyHostBuilder to read configuration bytes from _jsMethods.GetConfig(configFile) rather than File.ReadAllBytes.
5. Adds unit tests in WebAssemblyHostBuilderTest covering default and environment-specific appsettings loading without VFS.

Verification:
- 
pm test --workspace src/Components/Web.JS/ passed (all 14 test suites, 295 tests).
- dotnet test src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly/test/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Tests.csproj passed (all 59 tests).

Issues.Title: Inject services from a host-owned DI scope into Razor components
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Let a component resolve services from a DI scope owned by its host (for example the window that shows a
`BlazorWebView`), not only from the scope Blazor creates per page. Build it on a public version of the supplier
mechanism behind `[SupplyParameterFromQuery]`.

## Motivation and goals

In Blazor Hybrid the WebView usually lives inside something that already has a scope: a window, a dialog, a document.
That scope holds the state the UI works on, e.g. the order being edited. `WebViewManager` ignores it and renders each
page in a new scope (`_provider.CreateAsyncScope()` in `AttachToPageAsync`, again on every reload). `[Inject]` then
returns a new instance of any scoped service, and the component works on the wrong state without any error.

What you can do today:

- Pass each service as a root component parameter and cascade it. Works, but every service needs code in the host,
  the root component and the consumer, and dependencies end up as `[CascadingParameter]`s.
- Cascade the host `IServiceProvider` and resolve from it in a base class (`SetParametersAsync`). One cascade, but it
  is service location and forces a base class.
- Give the WebView a provider whose scope factory returns the host scope. Breaks on the second page load: `PageContext`
  gets the same `NavigationManager` back and `Initialize` throws `'WebViewNavigationManager' already initialized.`
- `AddCascadingValue(sp => ...)`: `sp` is the page scope, it can't see the host scope.
- Write a custom cascading attribute: not possible, `ICascadingValueSupplier` is internal and
  `CascadingParameterAttributeBase` only has internal members (10.0 and `main`).
- `IComponentActivator` / `IComponentPropertyActivator` (#64595): both work from the page scope, so they still need
  some link to the host scope.

A typical case: a desktop order-entry app opens a "New order" window per order. The window creates a scope with a
scoped `IOrderSession` (wrapping a `DbContext` and the order being edited) and hosts a `BlazorWebView` with the order
form. The form's components need *that* session. With `[Inject]` they get a new one, so edits go into a different
`DbContext` and the window's Save button doesn't see them. Every app in this situation ends up writing the same
attribute + cascade + base class. Third-party container integrations need the same pieces too: Simple Injector's
Blazor integration uses a `[Dependency]` attribute, a custom `IComponentActivator` and a required base component.

Goals:

- The component says where a dependency comes from, like `[FromKeyedServices]` does for parameters.
- Blazor's own scoped services stay per page; only the marked ones come from the host scope. Reloads keep working.
- Values are set before `OnInitialized`, like `[Inject]`. No base class.
- A missing scope or registration throws, with an error like `[Inject]`'s. No fallback to the page scope.
- Works with trimming and Native AOT.

## In scope

1. Blazor Hybrid: the host sets the scope once on the `BlazorWebView`, every component in it can use it.
2. A component that sets a scope for its subtree (e.g. a dialog).
3. Named scopes, for trees that need more than one.
4. A public supplier API for custom "value from X" attributes, which this feature is built on.
5. An analyzer and clear runtime errors.

## Out of scope

- Replacing or reusing Blazor's page scope. `NavigationManager`, `IJSRuntime` etc. must stay per page.
- Render-mode boundaries. A live scope can't go to WebAssembly or across prerendering.
- Nested scopes in Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.
- Constructor injection from the host scope (possible follow-up).

## Risks / unknowns

- Handing components the provider invites service location. Components should get values, never the provider.
- The host owns the scope. It can be disposed while the WebView still runs; that needs to be documented.
- Services from the host scope may be used from the renderer's dispatcher and from the host at the same time.
- A silent fallback to the page scope would bring back the original bug. Missing scope must throw.
- A public supplier API fixes part of the cascading pipeline in place. Keep it value-only, no `ComponentState`.
- It overlaps with `IComponentPropertyActivator`. This proposal uses cascading because that gives "nearest boundary"
  lookup and survives reloads; a property activator could still implement it.

## Examples

Host (WPF):

```csharp
var orderScope = scopeFactory.CreateAsyncScope(); // one per "New order" window

blazorWebView.Services = appServices;                         // page scopes come from here, as today
blazorWebView.HostServiceScope = orderScope.ServiceProvider;  // new
```

```xml
<blazor:BlazorWebView Services="{Binding AppServices}" HostServiceScope="{Binding OrderServices}" />
```

Component:

```csharp
public partial class OrderForm : ComponentBase
{
    [Inject]
    public NavigationManager Navigation { get; set; } = default!;   // page scope

    [InjectFromScope]
    public IOrderSession Order { get; set; } = default!;             // host scope

    protected override void OnInitialized() => Title = $"Order {Order.Current.Number}";
}
```

Scope for a subtree, and a named one:

```razor
<ServiceScopeBoundary Services="@DialogScope.ServiceProvider">
    <CustomerEditor />
</ServiceScopeBoundary>

<ServiceScopeBoundary Name="document" Services="@DocumentServices">
    <Editor /> @* [InjectFromScope("document")] IDocumentSession Session *@
</ServiceScopeBoundary>
```

The supplier API underneath, usable for other things:

```csharp
public sealed class FromTenantAttribute : SupplyParameterAttribute;

public sealed class TenantSupplier(ITenantAccessor tenants) : ParameterValueSupplier<FromTenantAttribute>
{
    protected override bool TryGetValue(in ParameterValueContext<FromTenantAttribute> context, out object? value)
    {
        value = tenants.Current?.GetSetting(context.PropertyType);
        return value is not null;
    }
}

builder.Services.AddParameterValueSupplier<FromTenantAttribute, TenantSupplier>();
```

Similar ideas elsewhere: `[FromServices]` / `[FromKeyedServices]`, MVC value providers, Simple Injector's
`[Dependency]`, Blazor's `[SupplyParameterFromQuery]`.

<!--
# Detailed design (sketch)

## Supplier API

- `public abstract class SupplyParameterAttribute : CascadingParameterAttributeBase`, optional `Name`. Discovery reuses
  the cascading-parameter code, including the trimming annotations.
- `public abstract class ParameterValueSupplier<TAttribute> where TAttribute : SupplyParameterAttribute`
  - `protected abstract bool TryGetValue(in ParameterValueContext<TAttribute> context, out object? value);`
  - `protected virtual bool IsFixed => true;`
  - Adapted to the internal `ICascadingValueSupplier`; `ComponentState` and subscriptions stay internal.
- `ParameterValueContext<TAttribute>`: attribute, property name and type, component type, nearest boundaries. Not the
  component instance.
- `services.AddParameterValueSupplier<TAttribute, TSupplier>()`, scoped like `AddCascadingValue`.

## Host scope

- `public sealed class InjectFromScopeAttribute(string? name = null) : SupplyParameterAttribute`
- `ServiceScopeBoundary` cascades an `IServiceProvider` (optionally named) without making it a plain
  `[CascadingParameter] IServiceProvider`.
- The built-in supplier resolves the property type from the nearest matching boundary. No boundary or no registration
  throws, e.g. "Cannot provide a value for property 'X' on type 'Y'. There is no service scope named 'Z' above it."
- Values are set before the first `SetParametersAsync`.
- `BlazorWebView.HostServiceScope` (WPF, WinForms, MAUI) wraps the root components in a boundary. Root components get
  their parameters again on every `AttachPage`, so this survives reloads.

## Drawbacks

- Two injection attributes to explain.
- More public API in the cascading pipeline.

## Alternatives considered

- Let the host replace the page scope: breaks reloads and mixes Blazor and host lifetimes.
- `[Inject(Scope = "...")]`: property injection runs before cascades exist, so it can't find the boundary without new
  plumbing.
- Make `ICascadingValueSupplier` public as is: leaks `ComponentState` and subscriptions, and every app rebuilds the
  same scope feature.
- `IComponentPropertyActivator` alone: gets the page scope, still needs the boundary.

## Open questions

- Constructor injection: `[FromScope]` on constructor parameters, like `[FromKeyedServices]`?
- Should `ServiceScopeBoundary` be able to create and dispose its own scope?
- Analyzer: `[InjectFromScope]` in components that can render on WebAssembly.

## References

- dotnet/aspnetcore#64595, #63451
- `WebViewManager.AttachToPageAsync`, `PageContext` (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebView)

Issues.Body: ## Description This PR partially addresses #69270 by fixing Blazor Server trimming and Native AOT warnings that have safe, framework-owned solutions. Issues.Title: Keep reconnected circuits alive after navigation interop timeouts
Issues.Body: ## Description This change prevents a server-side Blazor circuit from being terminated when a `NavigationManager.NavigateTo` JS interop call times out after a transient disconnect. Previously, a navigation request or reply lost while the SignalR connection was unavailable eventually raised a `TaskCanceledException`. Unless the circuit had been permanently disconnected, that exception reached the generic navigation failure path, raised `UnhandledException`, and terminated a circuit that could already have reconnected. The navigation flow now: - treats cancellation from a timed-out navigation interop call as a recoverable outcome for a live circuit; - logs the timeout as the `NavigationTimedOut` warning without raising `UnhandledException`; - continues to log navigation attempts on permanently disconnected circuits as `NavigationStoppedSessionEnded`; - preserves the existing failure behavior for unexpected JS interop errors. The regression coverage includes: - focused tests for live-circuit timeouts, permanently disconnected sessions, sessions ending during invocation, successful navigation, and unexpected errors; - a Selenium scenario that drops the real Blazor Server connection, issues navigation while disconnected, reconnects the same circuit, waits for the interop timeout, and verifies that the circuit remains interactive; - a browser control proving that unexpected navigation interop failures still display the error UI and disconnect the circuit. ## Output **Before** **After** Validation: ```text dotnet test src\Components\Server\test\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Tests.csproj --no-restore --filter "FullyQualifiedName~RemoteNavigationManagerTest" -p:UseIisNativeAssets=false -v:minimal Passed: 5, Failed: 0, Skipped: 0 dotnet build src\Components\test\E2ETest\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.csproj --no-restore -v:q -p:UseIisNativeAssets=false Build succeeded with 0 warnings and 0 errors dotnet test src\Components\test\E2ETest\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.csproj --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~NavigationReconnectionTest" Passed: 2, Failed: 0, Skipped: 0 ``` Fixes #69473

Issues.Title: Return 404 for missing mapped static assets
Issues.Body: ## Description This change fixes mapped static assets returning an empty `200 OK` response when the underlying file cannot be opened. Previously, `StaticAssetsInvoker` caught `FileNotFoundException`, cleared the response, and returned without setting an error status. Clearing the response reset its status to `200 OK` and removed its cache headers, allowing clients and intermediaries to cache the invalid response. This update: - Returns `404 Not Found` when a mapped static asset cannot be opened before the response starts. - Adds `Cache-Control: no-store` so the missing response is not cached. - Logs the missing mapped asset and its `FileNotFoundException`. - Preserves the existing static-web-assets configuration warning for build assets in production. - Allows assets to be served normally after a missing file is restored. - Avoids rewriting responses that have already started. - Handles missing uncompressed, compressed, and range-request representations. - Prevents the development runtime handler from reading metadata from a missing file. ### Output **Before** **After** ### Tests Added integration coverage for: - Missing mapped assets with and without development-time runtime reloading. - Missing build assets in production. - Assets deleted after first being served. - Missing compressed representations. - Range requests for missing assets. - Serving an asset after its file is restored. - Failures that occur after the response has started. - Missing-asset warning logs. Result: **Passed — 13 tests, 0 failures.** Fixes #69643

Issues.Title: Blazor Interactive Server: Component does not re-render after successful SignalR circuit reconnection and state notification
Issues.Body:
Blazor Interactive Server applications depend on SignalR connections to maintain interactive communication between the browser and server.

When network connectivity is interrupted temporarily, the browser may reconnect to an existing circuit. During the interruption, server-side application state may change independently of the disconnected client.

Although Blazor provides circuit reconnection and component rendering mechanisms, diagnosing state synchronization problems after reconnection can be difficult.

In particular, developers may need to determine whether:

- The original circuit was successfully recovered.
- The component remained subscribed to server-side state notifications.
- State changes occurred while the client was disconnected.
- A rendering notification was dispatched after reconnection.
- The component rendered successfully but displayed outdated application data.

These conditions can produce similar user-visible symptoms despite having different underlying causes.

It would be useful to improve the diagnostic information available for investigating state synchronization and rendering behavior after circuit reconnection.

This is an improvement proposal rather than a claim of a confirmed framework regression.

Issues.Title: CertificateAuthentication: CustomTrustStore/CustomRootTrust is not applied to self-signed client certificates
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`CertificateAuthenticationHandler` applies the configured custom trust (`CustomTrustStore` together with `ChainTrustValidationMode = CustomRootTrust`) only to certificates it classifies as chained. Certificates classified as self-signed are validated under a separate policy that never consults that configuration. When `AllowedCertificateTypes` includes `SelfSigned`, the trust options therefore do not describe a single, uniform trust boundary, and nothing tells the operator.

## What is wrong

* **Broken invariant:** when an app explicitly selects custom root trust and supplies a populated store, that store should be the set of roots the handler trusts for every certificate type it accepts. Today it applies to one type only.
* **Origin:** the self-signed branch in `BuildChainPolicy` predates `CustomTrustStore`. The store and trust mode were added later (#15029) to support chained certificates issued by a private CA, and the self-signed branch was not revisited. No test covers the combination of a self-signed certificate with `CustomRootTrust`.
* **Silent:** the combination is accepted without a log message or validation error.
* **Classifier:** the self-signed/chained decision is made by `IsSelfSigned()`, which compares subject and issuer names. It selects which validation policy runs, so the fix should not depend on its precision.

## Why it matters (defense in depth)

* **Correctness and least surprise:** the platform documents `X509ChainPolicy.CustomTrustStore` as "a collection of certificates replacing the default certificate trust". The handler's XML docs describe `CustomTrustStore` as "trusted components of the certificate chain" used in chain validation. Neither says self-signed certificates are exempt, so a reasonable reader expects the store to apply.
* **Hardening rationale:** the documentation already requires apps that accept self-signed certificates to pin them (thumbprint or issuer) in their own validation, see https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/security/authentication/certauth. Making the framework honor an explicitly configured trust store for self-signed certificates adds a second layer that does not rely on that app-side step being present.
* **Scope:** non-default configuration only. The default is `CertificateTypes.Chained` with system trust.

## Affected code

* src/Security/Authentication/Certificate/src/CertificateAuthenticationHandler.cs:204-252 - `BuildChainPolicy`
* src/Security/Authentication/Certificate/src/CertificateAuthenticationHandler.cs:228-233 - self-signed branch: sets `AllowUnknownCertificateAuthority` and `IgnoreEndRevocationUnknown`, does not apply `CustomTrustStore` or `TrustMode`
* src/Security/Authentication/Certificate/src/CertificateAuthenticationHandler.cs:234-242 - chained branch: the only place `CustomTrustStore` and `ChainTrustValidationMode` are applied
* src/Security/Authentication/Certificate/src/CertificateAuthenticationHandler.cs:118-146 - `ValidateCertificateAsync`: classification and `chain.Build`
* src/Security/Authentication/Certificate/src/X509CertificateExtensions.cs:19-24 - `IsSelfSigned` (name comparison)
* src/Security/Authentication/Certificate/src/CertificateAuthenticationOptions.cs:21-27 - `AllowedCertificateTypes` docs
* src/Security/Authentication/Certificate/src/CertificateAuthenticationOptions.cs:29-32 - `CustomTrustStore` docs
* src/Security/Authentication/Certificate/src/CertificateAuthenticationOptions.cs:38-46 - `ChainTrustValidationMode` docs
* src/Security/Authentication/Certificate/src/CertificateTypes.cs:17-25 - `SelfSigned` and `All` docs
* src/Security/Authentication/test/CertificateTests.cs:52-260 - existing self-signed tests (no custom-root coverage)
* src/Security/Authentication/test/CertificateTests.cs:319-386 - existing custom-root tests (chained only)

## Recommended fix

Deliver in two tiers. Tier 1 is non-breaking and can ship first, including to servicing branches. Tier 2 changes behavior and needs an owner decision on compatibility.

### Tier 1: documentation, signal, test coverage (non-breaking)

1. **Docs:** in the `AllowedCertificateTypes` and `CustomTrustStore` sections of the certificate authentication article, state that self-signed certificates are not evaluated against `CustomTrustStore`/`CustomRootTrust` and must be pinned by thumbprint or public key in `OnCertificateValidated` or an authorization policy. Move the pinning guidance out of the sample walkthrough into those sections. Mirror the note in the XML docs on `AllowedCertificateTypes`, `CustomTrustStore`, `ChainTrustValidationMode`, and `CertificateTypes.SelfSigned`.
2. **Startup signal:** log one warning per scheme, at options configuration time, when `AllowedCertificateTypes` includes `SelfSigned` and `ChainTrustValidationMode` is `CustomRootTrust` with a non-empty `CustomTrustStore`. Do not throw; the combination is legitimate for apps that accept private-CA chains and pin self-signed certificates themselves. Do not log per request.
3. **Tests:** add tests that pin current behavior for a self-signed certificate under `CustomRootTrust` so any later change is deliberate.

### Tier 2: apply custom root trust to self-signed certificates (behavior change)

* **Selected semantics:** define `useCustomRoot = ChainTrustValidationMode == CustomRootTrust && CustomTrustStore.Count > 0`.
  * When `useCustomRoot` is true, apply `CustomTrustStore` and `TrustMode` to every certificate, and do not set `AllowUnknownCertificateAuthority` for self-signed certificates. A self-signed certificate then validates only if it is present in the store.
  * When `useCustomRoot` is false, keep today's behavior unchanged.
  * Keep the existing self-signed handling for revocation (`NoCheck`, `IgnoreEndRevocationUnknown`), the `ExtraStore` additions, the client-auth EKU check, and the validity-period check.
  * The non-empty guard is required: with an empty store and `CustomRootTrust`, every self-signed certificate would fail.
* **Platform validation (Windows, .NET 10):**
  * With `CustomRootTrust`, a populated store, and `AllowUnknownCertificateAuthority` not set, a self-signed certificate validates only when it is in the store and otherwise fails with `UntrustedRoot`.
  * If `AllowUnknownCertificateAuthority` stays set, the store has no effect on a self-signed certificate, so the flag must be dropped in this mode.
  * Linux and macOS chain engines still need to be checked.
* **Independent of `IsSelfSigned`:** in `useCustomRoot` mode, trust no longer depends on the classification, so tightening the classifier is optional and separate.

**Alternatives considered**

* *Throw at startup for the combination:* rejected, it breaks legitimate setups that pin self-signed certificates in app code.
* *Tighten `IsSelfSigned` only:* rejected, it does not change trust semantics for a valid self-signed certificate.
* *Always apply trust to self-signed certificates, or drop `AllowUnknownCertificateAuthority` unconditionally:* rejected, it breaks all self-signed users on system trust.
* *Dedicated new option for self-signed trust:* viable, but it is new public API (API review required) and heavier than reusing the existing options.
* *Docs only:* insufficient on its own because the failure mode is silent.

**Compatibility and versioning**

* Tier 2 breaks apps that use `CustomRootTrust` with a populated store and `AllowedCertificateTypes` including `SelfSigned` and rely on self-signed certificates outside the store being accepted today.
* Owner decision needed: (a) opt-in first through an `AppContext` switch or a new option (a new public option requires the API review process and a `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` entry), then make it the default in the next major with a breaking-change article; or (b) make it the default in the next major only.
* Servicing branches: Tier 1 only.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] Tier 1 docs and XML docs state that self-signed certificates are not evaluated against `CustomTrustStore`/`CustomRootTrust` and need app-side pinning.
* [ ] A single warning per scheme is logged for the self-signed plus populated-custom-root combination, and nothing is logged for other combinations.
* [ ] Tests cover self-signed certificates under `CustomRootTrust` (certificate in store, certificate not in store, empty store) and the unchanged behavior under system trust.
* [ ] If Tier 2 is accepted: with `useCustomRoot`, a self-signed certificate outside the store is rejected and one inside the store is accepted; behavior without `useCustomRoot` is unchanged.
* [ ] Tier 2 behavior is verified on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
* [ ] The compatibility decision, any API review for a new option, and the breaking-change documentation are recorded before Tier 2 ships.

Issues.Title: ANCM aspnetcorev2.dll 20.0.26234.12 crashes w3wp with heap corruption (double free in FLS callback) when the worker process shuts down
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?
- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug
On an IIS server that hosts 12 in-process ASP.NET Core apps on .NET 10.0.12 (Hosting Bundle 10.0.12), `w3wp.exe` crashes
with `0xc0000374` (STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION) when a worker process shuts down. We see this on idle timeout,
on app pool recycle, and on config-change recycle. The Windows Event Log shows 335 such crashes in 30 days
(`Faulting module name: ntdll.dll, Exception code: 0xc0000374`). WAS event 5009 (exit code `0xc0000374`) ties them to
4 of the 12 ASP.NET Core app pools on the server; the other 8 pools have not logged this crash in the same period.

We captured full dumps with WER LocalDumps. Both dumps show the same thing: while IIS unloads the module during
`W3_SERVER::Terminate`, `FreeLibrary(aspnetcorev2.dll)` runs the DLL's process-detach routine, which calls `FlsFree`.
The FLS callback registered by `aspnetcorev2.dll` then frees a block that has already been freed.
`!analyze` reports `HEAP_CORRUPTION_ACTIONABLE_BlockNotBusy_DOUBLE_FREE_c0000374_ucrtbase.dll!_free_base`.

Requests are not affected, because the crash hits the old worker after IIS has already started a new one. But it
floods the event log, produces a WER report each time, and could trip Rapid-Fail Protection (5 crashes in 5 minutes)
on busy pools.

### Expected Behavior
The worker process shuts down cleanly when the app pool recycles or times out.

### Steps To Reproduce
1. Windows Server 2019 (10.0.17763), IIS 10, ASP.NET Core Hosting Bundle 10.0.12 (ANCM 20.0.26234.12).
2. Host any ASP.NET Core 10 app in-process (`hostingModel="inprocess"`). It happens with shadow copy on and off.
3. Leave the app pool on the default idle timeout (20 min), or recycle it manually (`appcmd recycle apppool`).
4. When the old worker exits, the Application log shows `w3wp.exe` faulting in `ntdll.dll` with `0xc0000374`.
   WAS logs event 5009 with exit code `0xc0000374`.

It does not happen on every shutdown, and only 4 of our 12 ASP.NET Core app pools are affected. We have not yet found what the affected pools have in common.

### Exceptions (if any)
Faulting thread (dump `w3wp.exe.29260.dmp`, captured right after "shutdown due to inactivity"):

```

ntdll!RtlReportCriticalFailure+0x97
ntdll!RtlpHeapHandleError+0x12
ntdll!RtlpHpHeapHandleError+0x7a
ntdll!RtlpLogHeapFailure+0x45
ntdll!RtlFreeHeap+0x96d20
ucrtbase!_free_base+0x1b
aspnetcorev2!RegisterModule+0x23aba          <- FLS callback
ntdll!RtlFlsFree+0xc7
KERNELBASE!FlsFree+0xb
aspnetcorev2!RegisterModule+0x23c9c
aspnetcorev2!RegisterModule+0x23869

aspnetcorev2!RegisterModule+0x22292

ntdll!LdrpCallInitRoutine+0x6f
ntdll!LdrpProcessDetachNode+0xf5
ntdll!LdrpUnloadNode+0x3f
ntdll!LdrpDecrementModuleLoadCountEx+0x71
ntdll!LdrUnloadDll+0x93

iiscore!MODULE_DLL::~MODULE_DLL+0x29
iiscore!MODULE_DLL::`vector deleting destructor'+0x14
iiscore!MODULE_DLL::DereferenceModuleDll+0x27
iiscore!MODULE_DLL::Terminate+0x3c

iiscore!IISCORE_PROTOCOL_MANAGER::StopListenerChannel+0x66

```

`FAILURE_BUCKET_ID: HEAP_CORRUPTION_ACTIONABLE_BlockNotBusy_DOUBLE_FREE_c0000374_ucrtbase.dll!_free_base`

A second dump (`w3wp.exe.52176.dmp`, logged by WAS as event 5011 "fatal communication error") has the same bucket and the same module versions.

Symbols for `aspnetcorev2.dll` did not resolve from the public symbol server, so frames show as `RegisterModule+offset`.

### .NET Version

Issues.Title: RouteHandlerAnalyzer: NullReferenceException (AD0001) when the handler is a delegate creation, `new Func<int, string>(Method)`, or a lambda under a cast
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

`RouteHandlerAnalyzer`, in the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Analyzers` assembly that ships in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref`, throws `NullReferenceException` on each of these two calls, and the build reports warning AD0001 for each:

```csharp
app.MapGet("/creation", new Func<int, string>(Handlers.Size));           // static string Size(int size)
app.MapGet("/converted", (Func<int, string>)(size => $"size {size}"));
```

The same handler passed as a method group (`Handlers.Size`), as a method group under a cast (`(Func<int, string>)Handlers.Size`) or as a lambda (`(int size) => ...`) is analyzed without an exception. The Request Delegate Generator plays no part: the warnings are the same with `EnableRequestDelegateGenerator` off and on. A lambda whose parameter is untyped needs such a cast: without it, `app.MapGet("/converted", size => $"size {size}")` is taken for a `RequestDelegate` and does not compile (CS0029, CS1662).

The analyzer looks for the handler twice, in two ways that disagree for these shapes:

- `DoOperationAnalysis` takes the first `IDelegateCreationOperation` under the handler argument and analyzes its target, a lambda or a method reference ([RouteHandlerAnalyzer.cs#L77-L90 at ad1e1ff](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteHandlers/RouteHandlerAnalyzer.cs#L77-L90), [RouteHandlerAnalyzer.cs#L105-L121](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteHandlers/RouteHandlerAnalyzer.cs#L105-L121)). Both calls above have one.
- The route's usage context, which the analyzer takes from `RouteUsageCache`, is built by `RouteUsageDetector.BuildContext`. It asks the semantic model for the symbol of the argument's expression, through `GetMethodInfo`, and returns `default` when that is not a method ([RouteUsageDetector.cs#L91-L96](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteEmbeddedLanguage/Infrastructure/RouteUsageDetector.cs#L91-L96), [RouteUsageDetector.cs#L333-L343](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteEmbeddedLanguage/Infrastructure/RouteUsageDetector.cs#L333-L343)). For an object creation of a delegate type, and for a cast whose operand is a lambda, `GetSymbolInfo` returns no symbol. `RouteUsageCache` keeps that `default(RouteUsageContext)` in a `RouteUsageModel` that is not null, since the route pattern itself was parsed ([RouteUsageCache.cs#L56-L76](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/Infrastructure/RouteUsageCache.cs#L56-L76)).

`DisallowNonParsableComplexTypesOnParameters` then calls `IsRouteParameter` for each parameter that gets that far, which leaves out the special types such as `HttpContext`, and `IsRouteParameter` reads `routeUsage.UsageContext.ResolvedParameters.FirstOrDefault(...)` ([DisallowNonParsableComplexTypesOnParameters.cs#L86-L95](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteHandlers/DisallowNonParsableComplexTypesOnParameters.cs#L86-L95), called at [L68](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteHandlers/DisallowNonParsableComplexTypesOnParameters.cs#L68)). In a default `RouteUsageContext`, `ResolvedParameters` is a default `ImmutableArray<ParameterSymbol>`, and `FirstOrDefault` throws on it: that is the frame at the top of the stack below. The three other readers of `ResolvedParameters` check `UsageContext.MethodSymbol` first: [RoutePatternAnalyzer.cs#L69-L73](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteEmbeddedLanguage/RoutePatternAnalyzer.cs#L69-L73), [RoutePatternHighlighter.cs#L55-L58](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteEmbeddedLanguage/RoutePatternHighlighter.cs#L55-L58) and [RoutePatternCompletionProvider.cs#L235-L237](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteEmbeddedLanguage/RoutePatternCompletionProvider.cs#L235-L237).

`release/10.0` has the same code at the same lines: [DisallowNonParsableComplexTypesOnParameters.cs#L86-L95 at 9aaf828](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9aaf828061dd5dc00e2dfeec654568e5ee0168ce/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteHandlers/DisallowNonParsableComplexTypesOnParameters.cs#L86-L95), [RouteUsageDetector.cs#L91-L96](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9aaf828061dd5dc00e2dfeec654568e5ee0168ce/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteEmbeddedLanguage/Infrastructure/RouteUsageDetector.cs#L91-L96), [RouteHandlerAnalyzer.cs#L77-L90](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9aaf828061dd5dc00e2dfeec654568e5ee0168ce/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteHandlers/RouteHandlerAnalyzer.cs#L77-L90) and [RouteUsageCache.cs#L56-L76](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9aaf828061dd5dc00e2dfeec654568e5ee0168ce/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/Infrastructure/RouteUsageCache.cs#L56-L76).

To check that reading, I built a project of 42 `Map` calls, each spelling the handler or the call another way, on both SDKs, with the generator off and on, and ran a small program that calls `SemanticModel.GetSymbolInfo` on the handler argument of each (Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.0.0, against the 10.0.12 reference assemblies). The same 24 calls get AD0001 in the four builds, and they are exactly the calls where `GetSymbolInfo` returns no symbol, the argument holds a delegate creation, and the handler has a parameter that reaches `IsRouteParameter`:

- a delegate creation: `new Func<int, string>(Handlers.Size)`, `new SizeHandler(Handlers.Size)` with a named delegate type, `new Func<int, string>((int n) => ...)` over a lambda;
- a lambda under a cast, whether its parameter is typed or not: `(Func<int, string>)(n => ...)`, `(Func<int, string>)((int n) => ...)`, `(Delegate)((int n) => ...)`, and an `async` one under `(Func<int, Task<string>>)`;
- a conditional expression or a switch expression of lambdas: `flag ? (int n) => "a" : (int n) => "b"`.

Nothing else I varied makes a difference: a default value on the parameter, a route parameter (`"/x"` or `"/x/{n}"`), the parameter's type among `int`, `string`, `int[]`, `object` and a record, `[FromQuery]` on it, the method among `MapGet`, `MapPost`, `MapPut`, `Map` and `MapFallback`, a route group as the builder, named arguments. There is no exception for a handler with no parameter (`new Func<string>(Handlers.Hello)`, `(Func<string>)(() => ...)`) or with `HttpContext` alone (`new Func<HttpContext, string>(Handlers.Ctx)`, `new RequestDelegate(Handlers.Raw)`), which never reach `IsRouteParameter`; nor for a method group, parenthesized or not, a lambda, parenthesized or not, a method group under a cast to `Func<int, string>`, to a named delegate type or to `Delegate`, and a delegate held in a local variable or in a readonly field.

What it costs, as far as I measured (the checks, in a second project built on both SDKs):

- The build succeeds with one AD0001 warning per such call. Under `TreatWarningsAsErrors` each one is an error and the build fails. On the console the diagnostic has no file and no line (`CSC : warning AD0001`); the call is named only in the whole message, which the compiler's error log has (`-p:ErrorLog=...`).
- For a call that throws, the checks that come after this one are not made ([the order, at L105-L121](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteHandlers/RouteHandlerAnalyzer.cs#L105-L121)). `app.MapGet("/b/{size?}", new Func<int, string>(Handlers.SizeB))` and `app.MapGet("/d/{size?}", (Func<int, string>)((int size) => ...))` get no ASP0007, and `new Func<int, IActionResult>(Handlers.MvcG)` gets no ASP0004. `app.MapPost("/k", new Func<Body, Body, string>(Handlers.TwoBodiesK))`, whose two parameters are `[FromBody]`, gets no ASP0024, which is an error by default. The same handlers passed as a method group or as a lambda get all three. ASP0003, which is checked before, is still reported.
- Two such calls on the same route get no ASP0022 either. That one is not lost to the exception: `DetectAmbiguousRoutes` leaves out a call whose usage context has no HTTP methods ([DetectAmbiguousRoutes.cs#L31](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteHandlers/DetectAmbiguousRoutes.cs#L31)), which is the case of a default one.
- The analyzer goes on with the other calls: in that project, a method group mapped after the nine calls that throw still gets its ASP0007.

Workaround: pass the method group, under a cast when the delegate type matters (`(Func<int, string>)Handlers.Size`), and type the lambda's parameter instead of casting the lambda (`(int size) => ...`). The repro's two calls rewritten that way build without a warning under `TreatWarningsAsErrors`. With the Request Delegate Generator on, see #69755 before adding such a cast: there it throws at the `Map` call for a method that has a default value. Otherwise, `<WarningsNotAsErrors>$(WarningsNotAsErrors);AD0001</WarningsNotAsErrors>` lets the build pass with the two warnings, and `<NoWarn>$(NoWarn);AD0001</NoWarn>` hides them, for every analyzer of the project. I ran the three on both versions.

### Expected Behavior

No AD0001: the repro builds without a warning, as it does when the same handler is passed as a method group or as a lambda. Either the usage context is built from the handler the analyzer has already found through the delegate creation, or the route parameter check is skipped when the usage context has no method, as the other readers of `ResolvedParameters` do.

### Steps To Reproduce

Repro project: https://github.com/AdCodicem/dotnet-upstream-repros/tree/main/aspnetcore-analyzer-routehandler-ad0001. `./repro.sh` builds it three times, as it is, with the generator on and with warnings as errors, and prints the AD0001 messages in full; `REPRO_TFM=net11.0 ./repro.sh` does the same on .NET 11. Nothing is run: the defect is in the build.

`Repro.csproj` (the repository's version takes the target framework from `REPRO_TFM`; `net10.0` is its default):

```xml

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
  </PropertyGroup>

</Project>
```

`Program.cs`:

```csharp

// RouteHandlerAnalyzer throws NullReferenceException on each of these two calls (warning AD0001).
app.MapGet("/creation", new Func<int, string>(Handlers.Size));
app.MapGet("/converted", (Func<int, string>)(size => $"size {size}"));

// The same handler as a method group and as a lambda: no exception.
app.MapGet("/group", Handlers.Size);
app.MapGet("/lambda", (int size) => $"size {size}");

app.Run();

static class Handlers
{
    public static string Size(int size) => $"size {size}";
}
```

```
dotnet build -p:UseSharedCompilation=false -p:ErrorLog=obj/build.sarif                                # 2 warnings AD0001, in full in obj/build.sarif
rm -rf bin obj && dotnet build -p:UseSharedCompilation=false -p:EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=true   # the same 2 warnings
rm -rf bin obj && dotnet build -p:UseSharedCompilation=false -p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=true            # 2 errors AD0001, exit code 1
```

`UseSharedCompilation=false` is not needed for the warning. It gives the build a compiler process of its own, which keeps the stack whole: through the compiler server, which is the default, the messages I got came without their two top frames, `FirstOrDefault` and `IsRouteParameter`, six builds in a row on SDK 10.0.401.

The first build, and the second one with the generator on, print the same thing (as `repro.sh` prints it: the warning and error lines, then the exit code):

```text

CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'Microsoft.AspNetCore.Analyzers.RouteHandlers.RouteHandlerAnalyzer' threw an exception of type 'System.NullReferenceException' with message 'Object reference not set to an instance of an object.'. [<repro>\Repro.csproj]
dotnet build: exit code 0
```

With `-p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`:

```text
CSC : error AD0001: Analyzer 'Microsoft.AspNetCore.Analyzers.RouteHandlers.RouteHandlerAnalyzer' threw an exception of type 'System.NullReferenceException' with message 'Object reference not set to an instance of an object.'. [<repro>\Repro.csproj]
dotnet build: exit code 1
```

### Exceptions (if any)

The second one is the same but for its `SyntaxNode` line, `SyntaxNode: app.MapGet("/converted", (Func< ... [InvocationExpressionSyntax]@[221..290) (4,0)-(4,69)`. The positions are zero-based: these are lines 4 and 5 of `Program.cs`. The character offsets are those of a file with LF line endings, which the repro's `.gitattributes` asks for; with CRLF they are `[161..222)` and `[225..294)`.

### .NET Version

### Anything else?

- Not new in .NET 10: the repro's `Program.cs` built for `net8.0` with the analyzer of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref` 8.0.25, on SDK 10.0.401, reports the same two warnings with the same top frames, and `release/8.0`, `release/9.0` and `release/11.0` have the same statement at line 92 (read at the head of each branch).
- Related, with other triggers: #56831 (closed; #61319 was closed as its duplicate) was a `NullReferenceException` from `ResolveParameterTypeSymbol`, in the same file, for a parameter whose type is a type parameter, fixed on `main` by #63641. #68976 (open) is an `IndexOutOfRangeException` for a method group from a referenced assembly, which its pull request #69260 traces to `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`, [line 47](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteHandlers/DisallowNonParsableComplexTypesOnParameters.cs#L47) of the same method; the diff of #69260 does not touch `IsRouteParameter`. Issues.Title: Request Delegate Generator: an intercepted `MapFallback` endpoint is registered with order 0 instead of `int.MaxValue`, and without its fallback metadata
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

Related: #65992 and its fix #67562, the previous `MapFallback` defect of the generator (the pattern was ignored), and #69757 (the two `MapFallback` overloads sharing one interceptor). This report is about what the interceptor registers, which neither of them covers.

With `EnableRequestDelegateGenerator` (on by default under `PublishAot` and `PublishTrimmed`), the endpoint that an intercepted `MapFallback` call registers is an ordinary route handler endpoint, not a fallback: its `Order` is 0 instead of `int.MaxValue`, its display name has no `Fallback ` prefix, and it carries no fallback metadata. The calls concerned are those to the two overloads that take a `Delegate`; the overloads that take a `RequestDelegate` are not intercepted. So the fallback no longer sorts after the other endpoints:

```csharp
app.MapGet("/{*path}", () => "catch-all");
app.MapFallback(() => "fallback");
```

With the generator off, `GET /missing` returns `catch-all`: the fallback has order `int.MaxValue` and sorts last. With the generator on, it returns `fallback`: both endpoints have order 0, so the route precedence decides, and a catch-all with a constraint (`{*path:nonfile}`) ranks before one without (`{*path}`). The build reports no warning and nothing throws.

`MapFallback(pattern, handler)` registers its endpoint with `isFallback: true`, and `MapFallback(handler)` calls it ([EndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs#L388-L422 at ad1e1ff](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/Builder/EndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs#L388-L422)). `RouteEndpointDataSource` derives three things from that flag: the order, `var order = isFallback ? int.MaxValue : 0;` ([RouteEndpointDataSource.cs#L135-L139](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/RouteEndpointDataSource.cs#L135-L139)), the `Fallback ` prefix of the display name ([#L157-L160](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/RouteEndpointDataSource.cs#L157-L160)) and `FallbackMetadata` ([#L186-L189](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/RouteEndpointDataSource.cs#L186-L189)).

The interceptor written for a `MapFallback` call ends, like every other one, in a call to `MapCore` ([RequestDelegateGenerator.Emitter.cs#L99-L117](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/RequestDelegateGenerator.Emitter.cs#L99-L117)), which calls `RouteHandlerServices.Map` ([RequestDelegateGeneratorSources.cs#L604-L614](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/RequestDelegateGeneratorSources.cs#L604-L614)), and that method passes `isFallback: false` to the data source ([RouteHandlerServices.cs#L79-L87](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/Builder/RouteHandlerServices.cs#L79-L87)). It has no parameter for it, and the generator writes nothing else that sets the order: what it does for `MapFallback` is choose the pattern (#67562) and pass `null` for the HTTP methods ([StaticRouteHandlerModel.Emitter.cs#L44-L60](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/StaticRouteHandlerModel/StaticRouteHandlerModel.Emitter.cs#L44-L60)). In the file generated for the repro, lines 232-239 and 253 on both versions:

```csharp
            return MapCore(
                endpoints,
                "{*path:nonfile}",
                handler,
                null,
                populateMetadata,
                createRequestDelegate,
                castHandler.Method);
```

```csharp
            return RouteHandlerServices.Map(routes, pattern, handler, httpMethods, populateMetadata, createRequestDelegate, methodInfo);
```

`RouteHandlerServices.Map` was written with `isFallback: false` (#46163, #46180) before the generator intercepted `MapFallback`, which #48012 added, for #47196, through the same method. It is still so: the files linked above are identical today on `main` (5c7435f) and on `release/11.0` (3c130d7), and `release/10.0` has the same code, [RouteHandlerServices.cs#L79-L87 at 9aaf828](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9aaf828061dd5dc00e2dfeec654568e5ee0168ce/src/Http/Routing/src/Builder/RouteHandlerServices.cs#L79-L87), [RequestDelegateGenerator.cs#L136-L153](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9aaf828061dd5dc00e2dfeec654568e5ee0168ce/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/RequestDelegateGenerator.cs#L136-L153), [RequestDelegateGeneratorSources.cs#L569-L579](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9aaf828061dd5dc00e2dfeec654568e5ee0168ce/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/RequestDelegateGeneratorSources.cs#L569-L579) and [RouteEndpointDataSource.cs#L135-L139](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9aaf828061dd5dc00e2dfeec654568e5ee0168ce/src/Http/Routing/src/RouteEndpointDataSource.cs#L135-L139). `release/8.0` and `release/9.0` have the same `isFallback: false` and the same `MapFallback` in the generator's list of methods; I read them and did not run them.

The documentation of both overloads says "The order of the registered endpoint will be `int.MaxValue`" and "with the lowest possible priority" ([EndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs#L367-L413](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/Builder/EndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs#L367-L413)).

Both overloads are affected, on a route group too. I ran each of the following as a project of its own, with the generator off and on, on 10.0.12 and on 11.0.0-rc.1, with the same answers on both:

- `app.MapGet("/{*path}", ...)` beside `app.MapFallback("/{*path:nonfile}", () => "fallback")`: the fallback has order 0 and answers `GET /missing`, as in the repro (on 10.0.12 its pattern is also replaced by `{*path:nonfile}`, which is #65992). The same in a group, with `api.MapGet("/{*path}", ...)` and `api.MapFallback(() => "api fallback")` on `app.MapGroup("/api")`.
- `app.Map("/{*path:nonfile}", () => "catch-all")` beside `app.MapFallback(() => "fallback")`: `GET /missing` returns `catch-all` with the generator off, and 500 with it on (`AmbiguousMatchException`, below). With `app.MapGet` in place of `app.Map`, the answer stays `catch-all`.
- A fallback that the generator does not intercept keeps `int.MaxValue`, so an intercepted one wins over it whatever the patterns. With `app.MapFallbackToFile("/admin/{*path:nonfile}", "admin.html")` and `app.MapFallback(() => "site fallback")`, `GET /admin/users` returns the file with the generator off and `site fallback` with it on. The same with a `RequestDelegate` overload, `app.MapFallback("/api/{*path}", (HttpContext context) => context.Response.WriteAsync("api fallback"))`: `GET /api/missing` returns `api fallback` with the generator off and `site fallback` with it on.
- An endpoint whose order is above 0 loses to it. With `AddControllers()`, `app.MapControllerRoute("default", "{controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}")` and `app.MapFallback(() => "fallback")`, `GET /`, `GET /Home/Index` and `GET /Home/Details/5` reach the controller with the generator off, and all three return `fallback` with it on: the endpoints of conventional routes are numbered from 1 ([OrderedEndpointsSequenceProvider.cs#L8-L19](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Mvc/Mvc.Core/src/Infrastructure/OrderedEndpointsSequenceProvider.cs#L8-L19)).
- Telemetry no longer sees a fallback: the measurement of `aspnetcore.routing.match_attempts` has `aspnetcore.routing.is_fallback=False` instead of `True`, and the debug log `Matched endpoint 'Fallback {*path:nonfile}' is a fallback endpoint.` is not written ([EndpointRoutingMiddleware.cs#L157-L172](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/EndpointRoutingMiddleware.cs#L157-L172)).

Workaround for the order: `app.MapFallback(() => "fallback").WithOrder(int.MaxValue);`. With the generator on, the endpoint then has order 2147483647, and the answers are those of the generator off in the repro and beside the `Map` catch-all, `MapFallbackToFile` and the conventional route above; I ran the four on both versions. The display name and the metadata stay those of an ordinary endpoint, and the metric still has `is_fallback=False`.

### Expected Behavior

With the generator on as with it off, the endpoint of `MapFallback` has order `int.MaxValue`, the display name `Fallback {*path:nonfile}` and the fallback metadata, and `GET /missing` returns `catch-all`.

### Steps To Reproduce

Repro project: https://github.com/AdCodicem/dotnet-upstream-repros/tree/main/aspnetcore-rdg-mapfallback-order. `./repro.sh` builds and runs it with the generator off, then on; `REPRO_TFM=net11.0 ./repro.sh` does the same on .NET 11.

`Repro.csproj` (the repository's version takes the target framework from `REPRO_TFM`; `net10.0` is its default):

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <EnableRequestDelegateGenerator>true</EnableRequestDelegateGenerator>
    <EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles>true</EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles>
  </PropertyGroup>

</Project>
```

`Program.cs` (it prints the order, the display name and the fallback metadata of each `RouteEndpoint`, then sends one request):

```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateSlimBuilder(args);
builder.Logging.ClearProviders();
builder.WebHost.UseUrls("http://127.0.0.1:0");
var app = builder.Build();

app.MapGet("/{*path}", () => "catch-all");
app.MapFallback(() => "fallback");

await app.StartAsync();
foreach (var endpoint in ((IEndpointRouteBuilder)app).DataSources.SelectMany(source => source.Endpoints).OfType<RouteEndpoint>())
{
    // FallbackMetadata is internal to Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing, hence the lookup by name.
    var fallbackMetadata = endpoint.Metadata.Any(metadata => metadata.GetType().Name == "FallbackMetadata");
    Console.WriteLine($"{endpoint.RoutePattern.RawText}: Order {endpoint.Order}, DisplayName \"{endpoint.DisplayName}\", FallbackMetadata {fallbackMetadata}");
}
using var client = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(app.Urls.First()) };
Console.WriteLine("GET /missing -> " + await client.GetStringAsync("/missing"));
await app.StopAsync();
```

```
dotnet build -p:EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=false && dotnet run --no-build -p:EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=false   # catch-all
rm -rf bin obj && dotnet build && dotnet run --no-build                                                                  # fallback
```

Output of `repro.sh` on SDK 10.0.401 with `net10.0`, after its first line, which names the SDK:

```text
== EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=false
/{*path}: Order 0, DisplayName "HTTP: GET /{*path}", FallbackMetadata False
{*path:nonfile}: Order 2147483647, DisplayName "Fallback {*path:nonfile}", FallbackMetadata True
GET /missing -> catch-all

== EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=true
/{*path}: Order 0, DisplayName "HTTP: GET /{*path}", FallbackMetadata False
{*path:nonfile}: Order 0, DisplayName "{*path:nonfile}", FallbackMetadata False
GET /missing -> fallback
```

The same output on SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 with `net11.0`.

### Exceptions (if any)

None in the repro: the other endpoint answers. Beside an endpoint that has the same order and the same precedence as the fallback and no HTTP method (`app.Map("/{*path:nonfile}", ...)`, second case above), the request fails with the generator on, on both versions. As printed by a middleware placed before `UseRouting()` that catches it, without that middleware's own frame:

```text
Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.Matching.AmbiguousMatchException: The request matched multiple endpoints. Matches:

/{*path:nonfile}
{*path:nonfile}
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.Matching.DefaultEndpointSelector.ReportAmbiguity(Span`1 candidateState)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.Matching.DefaultEndpointSelector.ProcessFinalCandidates(HttpContext httpContext, Span`1 candidateState)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.Matching.DefaultEndpointSelector.Select(HttpContext httpContext, Span`1 candidateState)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.Matching.DfaMatcher.MatchAsync(HttpContext httpContext)
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Routing.EndpointRoutingMiddleware.Invoke(HttpContext httpContext)
```

### .NET Version

10.0.401 (also 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128)

### Anything else?

- ASP.NET Core: 10.0.12 and 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 (the generator ships in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref`)
- No IDE (CLI); Windows 11 (10.0.26200) x64
- The generator was turned on with `EnableRequestDelegateGenerator` in a normal build. A project that sets `<PublishAot>true</PublishAot>` or `<PublishTrimmed>true</PublishTrimmed>` and not that property behaves the same with `dotnet build` and `dotnet run` (order 0, `GET /missing` returns `fallback`); I did not publish.
- What it changes in practice: nothing in the answers of an application whose other endpoints have order 0 and are made of literal and parameter segments, which rank before a catch-all at the same order. I ran `/`, `/items/{id}`, `/{slug}` and `/{section}/{slug}` beside a fallback, and the five requests I sent are answered the same with the generator on. The answer changes, silently, where the fallback meets an unconstrained catch-all endpoint, a fallback that is not intercepted, or an endpoint whose order is above 0, since the order is compared before the precedence ([EndpointComparer.cs#L27-L37](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/Matching/EndpointComparer.cs#L27-L37)) and a constrained catch-all ranks before an unconstrained one ([RoutePrecedence.cs#L272-L281](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/Template/RoutePrecedence.cs#L272-L281)). In every case the endpoint lacks the `FallbackMetadata` that the fallback log and the metric tag are read from.
- The tests of the runtime path assert what is lost here: `MapFallback_BuildsEndpointWithLowestRouteOrder` the display name and the order, `MapFallbackWithoutPath_BuildsEndpointWithLowestRouteOrder` the metadata too ([RouteHandlerEndpointRouteBuilderExtensionsTest.cs#L736-L769](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/test/UnitTests/Builder/RouteHandlerEndpointRouteBuilderExtensionsTest.cs#L736-L769)). The generator's three `MapFallback` tests assert the binding and the pattern, not the order ([RequestDelegateCreationTests.cs#L546-L609](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Http.Extensions/test/RequestDelegateGenerator/RequestDelegateCreationTests.cs#L546-L609)).
- About a fix: `RouteHandlerServices.Map` is public and has no parameter that says the endpoint is a fallback, and `FallbackMetadata` is internal ([FallbackMetadata.cs#L6](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/FallbackMetadata.cs#L6)). The `RequestDelegate` overload of `MapFallback` sets the display name, the order and the metadata through conventions ([FallbackEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs#L77-L81](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Routing/src/Builder/FallbackEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs#L77-L81)); generated code can set the order that way, as the workaround does, but cannot name the metadata type. I have not tried a fix.
- I found no report of this among the issues labelled `feature-rdg`, open or closed, nor with searches on `MapFallback` and the order, the priority, `isFallback` or `RouteHandlerServices`. The list of known issues that the generator's diagnostics link to (https://aka.ms/aspnet/rdg-known-issues) does not mention it.

Found while reviewing and testing #69752, the fix proposed for #69675. This defect does not depend on that pull request: the generators shipped in 10.0.12 and 11.0.0-rc.1 behave as shown above.

Investigation and write-up assisted by Claude (Anthropic); the linked repro was run on Windows 11, and I reviewed this report.

Issues.Title: Request Delegate Generator: a double parameter defaulting to -0.0 receives +0.0 (the generated fallback is the int expression -0); a decimal -0.0m loses its sign too
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

With `EnableRequestDelegateGenerator` (on by default under `PublishAot` and `PublishTrimmed`), a `double` parameter whose default value is `-0.0` receives `+0.0` when the request does not carry it. With the generator off it receives `-0.0`. One endpoint is enough:

```csharp
app.MapGet("/double", (double d = -0.0) => double.IsNegative(d) ? "-0.0" : "+0.0");
```

The generated fallback is `d_parsed_temp = -0;` (lines 120 and 158 of the generated file). `-0` is an `int` expression: its value is `0`, which converts to `+0.0`. The build reports no warning and nothing throws. I get the same `+0.0` for `double.NegativeZero`, for a `const`, for a `double?` parameter, for a method group, for a route value, for a `[FromHeader]` parameter and for a constructor parameter of an `[AsParameters]` record.

The text comes from the switch of `InnerGetDefaultValueString`, the helper behind `GetDefaultValueString` ([SymbolExtensions.cs#L262-L277 at ad1e1ff](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Shared/RoslynUtils/SymbolExtensions.cs#L262-L277)). A `float` is written as `SymbolDisplay.FormatPrimitive(f, false, false)` followed by `F`, a `decimal` the same way followed by `M`, and the infinities and NaN of both floating-point types have arms of their own. Any other `double` falls to the last arm, `SymbolDisplay.FormatPrimitive(defaultValue, false, false)`, with no suffix. Roslyn formats a `double` with `value.ToString("R", ...)` ([ObjectDisplay.cs#L490-L509 at 7ac1c03](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/7ac1c032ef132fa568d53459030089f17decf8aa/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/SymbolDisplay/ObjectDisplay.cs#L490-L509)), which gives `-0` here. A `double` whose text has neither a decimal point nor an exponent is therefore written as an integer literal (`0.0` gives `= 0;`); among the values I tried, that only matters for negative zero.

The emitter writes that text as it is, in the fallback ([EndpointParameterEmitter.cs#L149-L152](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/StaticRouteHandlerModel/Emitters/EndpointParameterEmitter.cs#L149-L152)) and in the delegate type of the cast ([StaticRouteHandlerModel.Emitter.cs#L28](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Http.Extensions/gen/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.RequestDelegateGenerator/StaticRouteHandlerModel/StaticRouteHandlerModel.Emitter.cs#L28)), which reads `Cast(handler, global::System.String (global::System.Double arg0= -0) => throw null!)` on line 181. That cast succeeds; only the fallback value is wrong. `release/10.0` has the same switch ([SymbolExtensions.cs#L220-L235 at 9aaf828](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9aaf828061dd5dc00e2dfeec654568e5ee0168ce/src/Shared/RoslynUtils/SymbolExtensions.cs#L220-L235)). The switch dates from #51193.

A `decimal` default of `-0.0m` loses its sign for a related reason: the fallback is `m_parsed_temp = 0.0M;`, because `decimal.ToString` does not print the sign of a negative zero. A `float` default of `-0.0f` keeps it: the fallback is `f_parsed_temp = -0F;`.

I compared the neighbouring literals the same way, generator off against generator on, on both versions: NaN, the infinities, `Epsilon`, `MaxValue` and `MinValue` of `double` and `float`, decimals of different scales (`1.0m`, `1.00m`, `0.00m`, `decimal.MaxValue`), escaped characters and strings (quotes, backslash, `\0`, `\n`, `\u2028`, a lone surrogate), `long.MinValue`, `ulong.MaxValue`, `int.MinValue` and bounds of the smaller integer types, and enum members (negative, undefined, `[Flags]`, `ulong`-based). Among those, only the two negative zeros differ.

The practical impact is small. `-0.0 == 0.0` is `true`, so only code that looks at the sign sees a difference (`1 / d`, `double.IsNegative`, formatting, which prints `-0`), and a default of negative zero is rare. For a `decimal` it is smaller still: `ToString` prints `0.0` either way, and only `decimal.IsNegative` or `decimal.GetBits` tell the two apart. I report it because the generator and `RequestDelegateFactory` silently disagree on the value a handler receives.

Workaround: a nullable parameter without a default value, and the default in the handler, `(double? d) => ...` reading `d ?? -0.0`.

### Expected Behavior

`GET /double` returns `-0.0` and `GET /decimal` returns `-0.0m`, as with the generator off.

### Steps To Reproduce

Repro project: https://github.com/AdCodicem/dotnet-upstream-repros/tree/main/aspnetcore-rdg-negative-zero-default. `./repro.sh` builds and runs it with the generator off, then on, then prints the fallbacks from the generated file; `REPRO_TFM=net11.0 ./repro.sh` does the same on .NET 11.

`Repro.csproj` (the repository's version takes the target framework from `REPRO_TFM`; `net10.0` is its default):

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <EnableRequestDelegateGenerator>true</EnableRequestDelegateGenerator>
    <EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles>true</EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles>
  </PropertyGroup>

</Project>
```

`Program.cs`:

```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateSlimBuilder(args);
builder.Logging.ClearProviders();
builder.WebHost.UseUrls("http://127.0.0.1:0");
var app = builder.Build();

app.MapGet("/double", (double d = -0.0) => double.IsNegative(d) ? "-0.0" : "+0.0");
app.MapGet("/float", (float f = -0.0f) => float.IsNegative(f) ? "-0.0f" : "+0.0f");
app.MapGet("/decimal", (decimal m = -0.0m) => decimal.IsNegative(m) ? "-0.0m" : "+0.0m");

await app.StartAsync();
using var client = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(app.Urls.First()) };
foreach (var path in new[] { "/double", "/float", "/decimal", "/double?d=-0" })
{
    Console.WriteLine($"GET {path} -> " + await client.GetStringAsync(path));
}
await app.StopAsync();
```

Output of `./repro.sh`:

```text
== .NET SDK 10.0.401, net10.0, MINGW64_NT-10.0-26200

== EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=false
GET /double -> -0.0
GET /float -> -0.0f
GET /decimal -> -0.0m
GET /double?d=-0 -> -0.0

== EnableRequestDelegateGenerator=true
GET /double -> +0.0
GET /float -> -0.0f
GET /decimal -> +0.0m
GET /double?d=-0 -> -0.0

== The fallbacks the generator wrote for -0.0, -0.0f and -0.0m (GeneratedRouteBuilderExtensions.g.cs)
d_parsed_temp = -0;
f_parsed_temp = -0F;
m_parsed_temp = 0.0M;
```

The output is the same on SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 with `net11.0`, its first line apart.

### Exceptions (if any)

None. The build and the run succeed; only the value differs.

### .NET Version

10.0.401 (also 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128)

### Anything else?

- ASP.NET Core: 10.0.12 and 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128 (the generator ships in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref`)
- No IDE (CLI); Windows 11 (10.0.26200) x64
- The theory `RequestDelegatePopulatesParametersWithDefaultValues` has had a `double.NegativeZero` row since #51193 ([RequestDelegateCreationTests.SpecialTypes.cs#L178](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Http.Extensions/test/RequestDelegateGenerator/RequestDelegateCreationTests.SpecialTypes.cs#L178)), and it passes for the generator. It compares with `Assert.Equal` ([#L261](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ad1e1fff7f0d9b9fa9b3cee789d62febcae496dd/src/Http/Http.Extensions/test/RequestDelegateGenerator/RequestDelegateCreationTests.SpecialTypes.cs#L261)), and `(-0.0).Equals(0.0)` is `true`.
- `-0D` and `-0.0M` are negative zeros: `double.IsNegative(-0D)` and `decimal.IsNegative(-0.0M)` are `true`. Writing a `double` with a `D` suffix, as a `float` is written with `F`, would therefore give it its sign back under the .NET SDK; the `decimal` needs its sign written explicitly.
- Not tested: a build whose compiler runs on .NET Framework. There `ToString("R", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)` returns `0` for a negative zero, `double` and `float` alike (checked in Windows PowerShell 5.1, on .NET Framework 4.8), so a `float` default may lose its sign as well. I could not build the repro with `MSBuild.exe`: my Build Tools installation does not resolve `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web`.
- Read, not run: `release/9.0` and `release/8.0` have the same `float`, `decimal` and last arms.
- Related: #51183 and its fix #51193, which wrote this switch; #51241, the follow-up on how default values are formatted; #63086, which added the enum cases. Not the grouping of #69675: a single endpoint shows it, and the generator built from #69752 gives the same `+0.0` on .NET 11.

Found while testing #69752, the fix proposed for #69675, which I reported from [AdCodicem.ValueObjects](https://github.com/AdCodicem/AdCodicem.ValueObjects). Investigation and write-up assisted by Claude (Anthropic); the linked repro was run on Windows 11, and I reviewed this report.
